sanskrit: eṣa vā odanaḥ sarvāṅgaḥ sarvātmā sarvaparuḥ sarvapāt sarvapṛṣṭhaḥ | sarvāṅgaḥ sarvātmā sarvaparuḥ sarvapāt sarvapṛṣṭho bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: This rice-oblation indeed is all-limbed, all-souled, all-jointed, all-footed, all-backed. All-limbed, all-souled, all-jointed, all-footed, all-backed becomes he who knows thus.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ viduṣa upadraṣṭā bhavaty upadraṣṭā prāṇaṃ ruṇaddhi | na ca prāṇaṃ ruṇaddhy atha sarvasvaṃ jīyate ||
english: He who becomes a witness-observer of one who knows thus — that witness-observer obstructs his vital breath. Yet he does not obstruct the vital breath, and then all his wealth is wrested away.

sanskrit: na ca sarvasvaṃ jīyate 'thainam āhāpratiṣṭhāno 'nāyatano mariṣyasīti | apratiṣṭhāna evānāyatano mriyate ya evaṃ viduṣa upadraṣṭā bhavati ||
english: And yet all his wealth is not wrested away — then one says to him: 'Thou shalt die, without foundation, without abode.' Without foundation indeed, without abode, does he die who becomes a witness-observer of one who knows thus.

sanskrit: kena pārṣṇī ābhṛte pūruṣasya kena māṃsaṃ saṃbhṛtaṃ kena gulphau | kenāṅgulīḥ peśinīḥ kena khāni kenocchṛṅkhau madhyataḥ kaḥ pratiṣṭhāḥ ||
english: By whom were the two heels of the man brought together? By whom was the flesh gathered? By whom the two ankles? By whom the fleshy toes, and by whom the apertures? By whom the two shin-bones raised up in the middle? Who is the foundation?

sanskrit: kasmān nu gulphāv adharāv akṛṇvann aṣṭhīvantā uttarau pūruṣasya | nirṛtya jaṅghe ni dadhuḥ kva svij jānunoḥ sandhī ka imau jajāna ||
english: Why indeed did they make the two ankles lower, and the two knee-caps upper, in the man? Having fashioned them, they set the two shanks in place — where then? Who begot these two joints of the knees?

sanskrit: catuṣṭayaṃ yujyate saṃhitāntaṃ jānubhyām ūrdhvaṃ śithiraṃ kabandham | śroṇī yad ūru ka u taj jajāna yābhyāṃ kusindhaṃ sudhṛtaṃ babhūva ||
english: A fourfold frame is joined together, holding at its seams, a loose trunk above the knees. The two haunches and the thighs — who then begot them? By means of those two the body became well and firmly held.

sanskrit: kati devāḥ katame ta āsan ya uraś cikyur agriyaṃ pūruṣasya | kati stanau ni dadhuḥ kaḥ kaphoḍau kati skandhān kati pṛṣṭīr acinvan ||
english: How many gods, and which were they, who built up the foremost chest of the man? How many set the two breasts in place? Who formed the two collar-bones? How many fashioned the shoulders, how many the ribs?

sanskrit: ko asya bāhū sam abharad vīryaṃ kṛṇavād iti | aṃsau ko asya tad devaḥ kusindha ā dadhād adhi ||
english: Who brought together his two arms, saying, 'Let him perform heroic deeds'? Which god placed his two shoulders upon the trunk and set them there?

sanskrit: mastiṣkam asya yatamo lalāṭaṃ kṛkāṭikāṃ prathamo yaḥ kapālam | citvā cityaṃ puruṣasya hanvor divaṃ ruroha katamaḥ sa devaḥ ||
english: Which one fashioned his brain, his forehead? Who first shaped the nape-joint and the skull? Having built the built-up structure of the man's two jaws, which god was it who ascended to heaven?

sanskrit: kaḥ sapta khāni vi tatarda śīrṣṇi karṇāv imāv akṣaṇī nāsike mukham | yeṣāṃ purutrā vijayasya mahmani catuṣpādo dvipādo yanti yāmam ||
english: Who pierced the seven apertures in the head — these two ears, the two eyes, the two nostrils, the mouth — whose greatness of conquest, in many places, both four-footed and two-footed creatures traverse?

sanskrit: hanvor hi jihvām adadhāt purūcīm adhā mahīm adhi śiśrāya vācam | sa ā varīvarti mahinā vyomann apo vasānaḥ ka u cit pra veda ||
english: He placed the tongue, widely extended, within the two jaws; thereupon he established mighty speech upon it. He rolls about in greatness in the sky, clothed in the waters — who indeed knows him fully?

sanskrit: mūrdhānam asya saṃsīvya- -atharvā hṛdayaṃ ca yat | mastiṣkād ūrdhvaṃ prairayat pavamāno 'dhi śīrṣṇaḥ ||
english: Having stitched together his head and that which is the heart, Atharvā sent the purifying breath upward from the brain, above the skull.

sanskrit: tad vā atharvaṇaḥ śiro devakośaḥ samubjitaḥ | tat prāṇo abhi rakṣatu śriyam annam atho manaḥ ||
english: That head of Atharvān is a divine casket, firmly clasped shut. May that vital breath protect the glory, the food, and likewise the mind thereof.

sanskrit: priyāpriyāṇi bahulā svapnaṃ saṃbādhatandryaḥ | ānandam ugro nandāṃś ca tān ud vahati pūruṣaḥ ||
english: The many pleasant and unpleasant things, sleep, oppression, torpor, delight, the vehement and its joys — all these does the man carry upward and bear forth.

sanskrit: ārtir avartir nirṛtiḥ kuto nu puruṣe 'matiḥ | rāddhiḥ samṛddhir avyṛddhir matir uditayaḥ kutaḥ ||
english: Distress, ill-fortune, dissolution — whence now in the man is lack of wisdom? Attainment, full prosperity, non-growth, intelligence, utterances — whence do these come?

sanskrit: ko asminn āpo adadhād viṣūvṛtaḥ purūcyutaḥ sindhusṛtyāya jātāḥ | tīvrāruṇā lohinīs tāmradhūmrā ūrdhvā avācīḥ puruṣe tiraścīḥ ||
english: Who placed the waters in him — flowing in diverse directions, falling in abundance, born to run like rivers? The fierce red ones, the bloody, the coppery-smoky, the upward-flowing and downward-flowing and transverse ones within the man.

sanskrit: ko asmin prāṇam adadhāt ko apānaṃ vyānam u | samānam asmin ko devo 'dhi śiśrāya pūruṣe ||
english: Who placed the in-breath in him, who the out-breath, and likewise the diffused breath? Which god established the equalizing breath upon this man?

sanskrit: ko asmin rūpam adadhāt ko mahmānaṃ ca nāma ca | gātuṃ ko asmin kaḥ ketuṃ kaś caritrāṇi pūruṣe ||
english: Who placed form in him? Who greatness and a name? Who placed gait in him, who the distinguishing mark, who the deeds of conduct in the man?

sanskrit: ko asmin reto adadhāt tantur ā tāyatām iti | medhāṃ ko asminn adhy auhat ko bāṇaṃ ko nṛto dadhau ||
english: Who placed seed in him, saying, 'Let the thread be extended'? Who poured wisdom upon him? Who placed the arrow in him, who the masculine vitality?

sanskrit: ko vāsasā pary adadhāt ko asyāyur akalpayat | balaṃ ko asmai prāyacchat ko asyākalpayaj javam ||
english: Who clothed him with a garment? Who ordained his lifespan? Who bestowed strength upon him? Who ordained his swiftness?

sanskrit: ko asmin yajñam adadhād eko agre adhi pūruṣe | ko asmin satyaṃ ko 'nṛtaṃ ko mṛtyuṃ ko 'mṛtaṃ dadhau
english: Who first, as the one, placed sacrifice upon this man? Who placed truth in him, who falsehood, who death, who immortality?

sanskrit: kenāpo anv atanuta kenāhar akṛṇod ruce | uṣasaṃ kenānvaindha kena sāyaṃbhavaṃ dade ||
english: By whom were the waters spread out in sequence? By whom was the day made for brilliance? By whom was the dawn kindled? By whom was the evening-born given?

sanskrit: kenemāṃ bhūmim aurṇot kena pary abhavad divam | kenābhi mahnā parvatān kena karmāṇi pūruṣaḥ ||
english: By whom was this earth covered over? By whom did he encompass the sky? By whom in greatness the mountains? By whom does the man perform his deeds?
